entries.title: Job 13:1
segments: All this; God's dealings, in his providence, with both the righteous and the wicked.

entries.title: Job 13:3
segments:
Reason with God; and not men, about the cause of my calamities. 
 
When the soul is conscious of integrity and duly feels its dependence on God, it will look to him, rather than to men for help, feeling that he alone can grant relief.

entries.title: Job 13:4
segments:
Forgers of lies; they gave a false view of the reasons of his afflictions. 
 
  Physcians of no value; they did not apply the right remedy to his case, nor in the least assuage his anguish.

entries.title: Job 13:7
segments: Speak wickedly for God; attempt to justify his ways by falsehood in respect to me.

entries.title: Job 13:8
segments: Will ye accept his person? show partiality towards him at the expense of truth and righteousness; as if he and his government needed to be defended by such means.

entries.title: Job 13:9
segments:
Is it good; will it result in your good? 
 
  Search you out; make manifest the unrighteousness of your proceedings under the pretence of honoring him. 
 
  Mock him; they mock God who defend his dealings towards men by falsehood and unjust accusations of their brethren. 
 
God does not need falsehood in his creatures to vindicate his dealings; and those who are guilty of it, whatever be their motives, will fall under his righteous displeasure.

entries.title: Job 13:10
segments: Secretly accept persons; see note to

entries.title: Job 13:12
segments:
Remembrances; here probably in the sense of maxims of wisdom. 
 
  Your bodies to bodies of clay; or, your bulwarks are bulwarks of clay; that is, your boasted arguments amount to nothing.

entries.title: Job 13:14
segments: Take my flesh in my teeth; the same as, put my life in my hand; that is, expose myself to the loss of life by speaking boldly,
.  The reason why he does this is, that he must speak, whatever shall be the result.

entries.title: Job 13:15
segments:
Maintain mine own ways; show his integrity, and that he was not a hypocrite. 
 
Confidence in God is the grand safeguard in trouble, and a preparation for deliverance from it.

entries.title: Job 13:18
segments: Shall be justified; proved to be innocent of the charges which they made against him.

entries.title: Job 13:19
segments: Who is he that will plead with me? a passionate expression of his desire to find one who understands his cause, and with whom he can argue it.  That one can be no other than God.

entries.title: Job 13:20
segments: Do not two things; continue not his distresses, nor overawe him with His majesty,

entries.title: Job 13:21
segments: God can so afflict the soul and overawe it with his presence as entirely to unfit it to commune with him, or experience the benefit of calling upon him in spirit and in truth.

entries.title: Job 13:23
segments: Mine iniquities; for which he was so dreadfully afflicted.

entries.title: Job 13:26
segments:
Possess the iniquities of my youth; be punished for sins committed when young. 
 
Sins committed in early life may be the means of great sufferings in age, which shall continue till those who committed them go down to the grave.

entries.title: Job 13:27
segments: Puttest my feet--in the stocks; confined him by sickness as really as if put in the stocks.

entries.title: Job 13:28
segments: And he; man.  Here Job passes from the consideration of his own calamities to that of the common miseries of man.  See the following chapter.
